extracted.intended_audience: Prospective bidders, lessees, and other stakeholders in the BOEM NY Bight offshore wind lease sale (offshore wind developers, legal/finance/compliance teams, and their representatives)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive requirements, deadlines, forms, financial assurances, lease terms, and auction mechanics for participating in the BOEM NY Bight commercial offshore wind lease sale. Covers bidder qualification, the BFF and bid deposit, auction format and rules, lease terms/stipulations, and post-auction steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public seminar publication and attendance
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM will host a public seminar to discuss the lease sale process and the auction format. The time and place will be announced by BOEM and published on the BOEM website. No registration or RSVP is required to attend.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Website: https://www.boem.gov/NY-Bight/.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission deadline for qualification materials
rubrics_metrics.description: All qualification materials must be received by BOEM by the end of the 60-day PSN comment period (August 13, 2021).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Materials must be sufficient to establish a company's legal, technical, and financial qualifications pursuant to 30 CFR 585.106-.107.

rubrics_metrics.name: BOEM review of PSN comments
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM will review all comments submitted in response to the PSN during the comment period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finalize bidder qualifications before FSN
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to publication of the FSN, BOEM will complete any outstanding reviews of bidder qualifications materials submitted during the PSN comment period and publish the final list of eligible bidders in the FSN.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare and publish FSN
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM will prepare the FSN by updating information contained in the PSN where appropriate and will publish the FSN in the Federal Register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bidder's Financial Form (BFF) submission timing and method
rubrics_metrics.description: Each bidder must submit a BFF to BOEM in order to participate in the auction; BOEM must receive each bidder's BFF no later than the date listed in the FSN. New BFFs must be submitted for this auction (previous BFFs are not acceptable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BFF downloadable at https://www.boem.gov/NY-Bight/. Until further notice, BFFs may be submitted electronically in PDF to renewableenergy@boem.gov; digital signatures on paper and digital copies are acceptable. Accompany submissions with a transmittal letter on company letterhead; BOEM prefers bidders use a company email address on their BFF. The BFF must be executed by an authorized representative listed on the bidder's legal qualifications and include a self-certification per 18 U.S.C. 1001. BOEM will consider the date an emailed submission was sent to the OREP mailbox as the official receipt date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bid deposit amount and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Each bidder must provide a bid deposit of $5,000,000; if the FSN allows bidders to win up to two lease areas, a $10,000,000 bid deposit is required to bid on two leases. Bid deposits are due no later than the date listed in the FSN to participate in the mock auction and the monetary auction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BOEM will consider extensions only if failure to timely submit was caused by events beyond bidder's control. Further information in the “Bid Deposit” section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mock auction participation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM will hold a mock auction open only to qualified bidders who have met the requirements and deadlines for auction participation, including submission of the bid deposit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final details of the mock auction will be provided in the FSN.

rubrics_metrics.name: Auction timing and provisional winners announcement
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM will hold a monetary auction as described in the FSN no sooner than 30 days following publication of the FSN in the Federal Register; estimated timeframes assume auction will occur ~45 days after FSN publication. BOEM will announce provisional winners after the auction ends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final dates included in the FSN.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refunds and explanations to non-winners
rubrics_metrics.description: Once provisional winners have been announced, BOEM will provide non-winners with a written explanation of why they did not win and return their bid deposits.

rubrics_metrics.name: DOJ antitrust review period
rubrics_metrics.description: Department of Justice will have 30 days to conduct an antitrust review of the auction pursuant to 43 U.S.C. 1337(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Delivery of lease copies and first year's rent due
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM will send three copies of the relevant lease to each winner, with instructions on how to execute the lease. The first year's rent is due 45-calendar days after the winner's receipt of the lease copies for execution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Return of lease within 10-business days and required actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 10-business days of receiving the lease copies, auction winners must post financial assurance, pay any outstanding balance of their bonus bids (winning bid minus applicable bid deposit), and sign and return the three lease copies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Winners may request extensions to the 10-day deadline and BOEM may grant such extensions if delay caused by events beyond winner's control, pursuant to 30 CFR 585.224(e). If BOEM has received signed lease copies and verified required materials, BOEM will determine issuance and execute each lease.

rubrics_metrics.name: BOEM's right to withdraw blocks
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM reserves the right to withdraw all or portions of the Lease Areas prior to executing the leases with the winning bidders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of proposed lease terms and attachments
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM has made available proposed terms, conditions, and stipulations for the leases and the lease includes seven attachments (Addenda A–E and Appendices A–B).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addenda A, B, and C provide detailed descriptions; D filled at COP approval; E after COP approval. Final terms will be published in the FSN after considering comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required plans timing: SAP and COP
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 30 CFR 585.601, if site assessment activities will be conducted, lessee must submit a Site Assessment Plan (SAP) within 12 months of lease issuance; to continue commercial lease with an operations term, lessee must submit a Construction and Operations Plan (COP) at least 6 months before the end of the site assessment term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fisheries Communication Plan (FCP) timing requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The amended FCP requirement specifies that the FCP must include discussions with fisheries stakeholders regarding any planned facilities within 120 days of lease execution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Native American Tribes Communication Plan (NATCP) and Tribal Liaison
rubrics_metrics.description: Lessee must develop a NATCP including designation of a Tribal Liaison responsible for communicating with Federally recognized Tribes, provide BOEM and Federally recognized Tribes with a draft NATCP, and meet with Federally recognized Tribes to discuss the NATCP within 120 days of lease execution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protected species mitigation alignment with NMFS IHAs
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM proposes that lease stipulations no longer specify exclusion zones for sound propagation from geophysical survey equipment, vessel strike avoidance measures, or protected species observer procedures; mitigation measures adopted during consultation rely upon up-to-date science and mirror recent IHAs, reducing requests to modify lease stipulations to be consistent with respective NMFS-issued IHAs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BOEM intends to finalize programmatic informal consultation with NMFS before the FSN; these measures aim to reduce compliance burdens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Site characterization pre-survey meeting discretion
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM recommends changing the requirement for a pre-survey meeting with the lessor to be at BOEM's discretion and removing the requirement for the lessee to meet with BOEM prior to holding Tribal pre-survey meetings to allow more scheduling flexibility and greater opportunity for Tribal input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Siting conditions prohibiting surface facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Lease stipulations outline situations where the lessee may not construct surface facilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operating fee simplifications and capacity formulation
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM proposes several simplifications to the operating fee: eliminating the inflation adjustment, moving from a weighted peak/off-peak power price to a simple hourly average, and eliminating the 10 percent limit to the capacity adjustment every five years. BOEM proposes to use the nameplate capacity in the Fabrication and Installation Report (FIR) rather than the COP for the operating fee calculation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changes are designed to simplify calculation with minimal impact on revenues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Labor Agreement (PLA) stipulation
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM proposes adding a lease stipulation requiring the lessee to make every reasonable effort to enter into a project labor agreement covering the construction stage of any project proposed for the leased area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This responds to Executive Order 14008 and supports OCS Lands Act factors (expeditious development, safe operations, safety, fair return) by promoting labor stability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stakeholder and Ocean User Engagement Summary reporting requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Lessee must include a stakeholder and ocean user engagement summary as part of progress reporting requirements, describing all existing users, engagement activities during the reporting period, and efforts to minimize conflicts between existing users and the lessee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See section 2.2 of addendum C of the lease.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rent: first-year payment and calculation for portions not in commercial operations
rubrics_metrics.description: First year's rent payment of $3 per acre is due within 45-calendar days of lessee receiving the lease for execution. Once commercial operations begin, BOEM charges rent only for portions of the leased area not authorized for commercial operations; fraction is based on nameplate capacity not yet authorized divided by maximum COP capacity, multiplied by $3/acre × acres.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example provided calculating prorated rent; if COP does not propose commercial activities for entire area, those portions pay $3/acre. If lessee relinquishes portion within 45 days after receipt, no rent for relinquished portion; later relinquishments reduce rent starting the following year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rent for project easement and additional acreage
rubrics_metrics.description: Lessee must pay rent for any project easement commencing on the date BOEM approves the COP describing the easement. Annual rent for a project easement 200 feet wide centered on the transmission cable is $70 per statute mile. For additional acreage required, lessee must pay the greater of $5 per acre per year or $450 per year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operating fee calculation and parameters
rubrics_metrics.description: Subsequent annual operating fee payments are calculated by multiplying the operating fee rate by the imputed wholesale market value of projected annual electric power production; the imputed market value equals nameplate_capacity × 8,760 hours × capacity_factor × annual_average_price (from a regional wholesale power price index).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial annual operating fee applies a rate to a proxy for wholesale market value and is prorated for the first year; subsequent payments due on or before each Lease Anniversary. BOEM proposes operating fee rate of 0.02 (2%) for the life of commercial operations and proposes to use the simple average of spot price indices for NYISO Zone J for the wholesale power price.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nameplate capacity definition for operating fee
rubrics_metrics.description: Nameplate capacity is the maximum rated electric output, expressed in MW, which the turbines of the wind facility under commercial operations can produce at rated wind speed as designated by the turbine's manufacturer. Nameplate capacity at the start of each year is the capacity provided in the FIR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 100 turbines × 12 MW each = 1,200 MW.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capacity factor specification and adjustment schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: Capacity factor is the decimal (0–1) representing energy delivered vs theoretical full capacity; for this lease the capacity factor for the commercial operation year and first six full years is set to 0.4 (40%). At the end of the sixth year, the capacity factor may be adjusted based on performance over the previous five years using metered electricity at delivery point; similar adjustments may be made every five years thereafter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasons for <100% include wind availability, transmission loss, downtime for maintenance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wholesale power price index selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 30 CFR 585.506(c)(2)(i), the wholesale power price (dollars/MWh) is determined at the time each annual operating fee payment is due. For these leases, BOEM proposes to use the simple average of the spot price indices for NYISO New York City (Zone J).

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial financial assurance requirement and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 10-business days after receiving lease copies, provisional winners must provide an initial, lease-specific bond or other approved means of meeting initial financial assurance requirements in the amount of $100,000 (pursuant to 30 CFR 585.515-.516).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Financial assurance may be a surety bond or an escrow account with a trust agreement giving BOEM withdrawal rights. BOEM encourages discussion of requirements as soon as possible after the auction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial assurance for SAP, COP, and decommissioning determined case-by-case
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM will base the amount of all SAP, COP, and decommissioning financial assurance on cost estimates for meeting all accrued lease obligations at each development stage. Required amounts of supplemental and decommissioning financial assurance will be determined on a case-by-case basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: BFF completion and original executed copy requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Each bidder must fill out the BFF referenced in the PSN; BOEM recommends designating an email in the BFF for creating a pay.gov account. BOEM will not consider prior BFFs for this auction. BOEM will only accept an original, executed paper copy of the BFF executed by an authorized representative listed in the qualifications package.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bid deposit application, refunds, and retention rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Bid deposits are applied against the high bonus bid obligation after the auction; if deposit exceeds total financial obligation, BOEM refunds the balance. BOEM refunds deposits to non-winners once provisional winners announced. If a provisional winner fails to timely return signed lease, establish financial assurance, or pay bid balance, BOEM will retain that provisional winner's deposit and may determine which bid would have won absent the non-compliant winning bid and offer lease to next highest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum bid amount
rubrics_metrics.description: The minimum bid is the lowest bid BOEM will accept as a winning bid and the starting price in the auction. BOEM proposes a minimum bid of $100.00 per acre for this lease sale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Auction format: ascending bidding with cash bid variable
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM proposes to use an ascending bidding auction with cash as the bid variable, starting at minimum bid prices and increasing incrementally until no more than one active bidder per Lease Area remains.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BOEM discusses alternative formats and recommends simultaneous ascending clock auction as best practice for allowing bidders to monitor activity and adjust choices; BOEM may choose format in FSN.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simultaneous vs sequential auction rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM explains sequential auctions introduce random and opaque valuations, strategic complexity, inability to accommodate substitutes/complements, and are more likely to lead to gamesmanship and inefficient outcomes. In contrast, simultaneous ascending clock auctions allow real-time monitoring and adjustment and are supported by academic literature as best practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Auction rule — bidding when bidders allowed to win only one lease area
rubrics_metrics.description: If bidders may win only one lease area: auction conducted in rounds; BOEM states asking price for each area each round; a 'live bid' equals asking price; to participate in next round a bidder must have submitted a live bid (or have carried-forward bid) in each previous round. BOEM raises asking price for areas that had two or more live bids; bidders generally free to bid on any of eight areas unless previous bid was uncontested, in which case it is carried forward and bidder cannot switch unless contest arises; disclosure between rounds: number of live bids per area and next-round asking prices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exit bids (intra-round bids) can be submitted after first round only for the same contested lease; exit bid is higher than previous asking but less than current asking, is not visible to other bidders, and is final for that bidder; a lease area with only exit bids will not have asking price raised. Provisionally-winning bids determined by two-stage procedure: Stage 1 highest bid in final round; Stage 2 choose combination maximizing sum subject to constraints (tie-breaking by pseudorandom numbers). Bidders may be bound by bids until auction results finalized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Auction rule — bidding when bidders allowed to win two lease areas
rubrics_metrics.description: If bidders may win up to two lease areas: auction conducted in rounds; bidders may submit a 'live bid' for up to two Lease Areas based on eligibility (two, one, or zero) determined by bid deposit ($5M for one-lease eligibility, $10M for two-lease eligibility). A bidder's eligibility in subsequent rounds is based on number of lease areas in its live bid from prior round (eligibility can stay same or go down but cannot increase). Uncontested live bids are carried forward and prevent other bidding by that bidder until contest arises. Between rounds BOEM discloses number of live bids and next-round asking prices. Intra-round bids function similarly to exit bids but have special rules when bidding two areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intra-round bids are private to BOEM, not considered live for concluding the auction or raising asking prices. Examples provided showing numeric bounds for intra-round offers; placing intra-round bids can reduce future bidding eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bidder eligibility mechanics and deposits determining eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: A bidder's initial eligibility to bid on one or two lease areas is determined by the amount of bid deposit: $5,000,000 for one-lease eligibility; $10,000,000 for two-lease eligibility. A bidder's eligibility changes based on the number of lease areas included in its live bid in the prior round and can decrease (never increase) as the auction proceeds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bid deposit used as down payment on monetary obligations if awarded a lease.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intra-round/exit bid properties and visibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Exit (intra-round) bids are single-offer prices greater than previous round asking but less than current round asking, are private (visible only to BOEM), are not live bids, and are final offers for that bidder. They do not trigger asking price increases and are not used to determine whether auction concludes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules limit when a bidder may submit exit/intra-round bids (only on same contested lease(s) from prior round) and whether submitting such bids affects future eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisionally-winning bid determination (two-stage selection)
rubrics_metrics.description: After bidding ends BOEM determines provisionally-winning bids via two stages: Stage 1 — designate the highest bid (live or exit) for each lease area in the final round as provisionally-winning if single highest; ties among identical highest exit bids deferred to Stage 2. Stage 2 — consider bids from all rounds for lease areas not assigned in Stage 1 from bidders not assigned in Stage 1 and select combination maximizing sum of selected bids subject to: (1) lease areas with multiple highest exit bids assigned to one of those bidders, (2) at most one bid per bidder selected, and (3) at most one bid per lease area selected. If unique combination, those are remaining provisional winners; tied combinations resolved by pseudorandom numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisional winners pay the amounts of their provisionally-winning bids.
